title: Malik al-Mulk
tomorrow: Eli comes to apologize. how do you take it without shrinking him?

lines: A KEYRING: WHAT WE CALL MINE.
cards: Keys. A house key, a car fob, a little one for a bike lock or a locker. A keyring is a short list of everything we call mine.
Yesterday's question came from a thirteen-year-old with a spray can, who said a wall belongs to whoever paints it. That's wrong.
But it's a crooked version of a real question, one the Qur'an asks out loud: whose is anything, really?

teach.b: Today's Name is Malik al-Mulk, Owner of All Sovereignty. Mulk is having in every size: a throne, a kingdom, a corner store, a set of keys.

Here's the verse, in Pickthall's words: "Say: O Allah! Owner of Sovereignty! Thou givest sovereignty unto whom Thou wilt, and Thou withdrawest sovereignty from whom Thou wilt. Thou exaltest whom Thou wilt, and Thou abasest whom Thou wilt. In Thy hand is the good. Lo! Thou art Able to do all things."
Notice the first word, Qul, say. This verse is written to be spoken. So, the wall.
And in the deepest sense it isn't fully the owner's either: what anyone holds is given, and can be withdrawn.
That doesn't make the wall fair game. It makes the owner a caretaker, holding something on loan, and a borrowed thing gets more care, not less. And here's a detail to tell a friend tonight.
The verse lists giving and taking, raising and lowering.

teach.h: IN THY HAND IS THE GOOD.
teach.b: Then it says only: in Thy hand is the good.
Some commentators notice that it names the good alone, and read that as courtesy in how we speak to God.

how: Some Muslims recite 3:26 as a supplication; it opens with qul, say, so it is meant to be spoken aloud.

o: the Lord who makes people wealthy
the King of the angels in heaven
Owner of all sovereignty and power

games.q: the verse of the open hand — tap the pairs.

s: if everything belongs to God, then nothing belongs to anyone, so taking is fine
what's held on loan is a trust: the holder cares for it more, not less.
3:26 begins with qul, say, so it is meant to be spoken
the verse says both the good and the bad are in His hand
it says only: in Thy hand is the good. some commentators read that as courtesy toward God.

games.q: you get the lead in the spring play. your friend who wanted it is crushed. how does 3:26 have you hold the part?
o: you earned it, fair and square, so it's simply and fully yours.
as given, and able to be withdrawn: hold it with care, gently.
hand it to your friend, since nothing is really yours anyway.
games.why: the verse says sovereignty is given and withdrawn. that doesn't mean giving it away; it means holding it like something on loan.

practice: Take your keys, or any small thing you'd call yours, and rest it in an open palm. Say the verse's first and last lines aloud, slowly: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, and, in Thy hand is the good.
Then leave your hand open, the thing resting there and not gripped, for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Malik al-Mulk. Owner of All Sovereignty: the One who gives every kind of having, and takes it back.

orig.note: Arabic: Owner of Sovereignty, the opening address of 3:26.

carryVoice: Carry this: owner of all, and everything on your keyring held on loan, with care. Fifteen fifty-eight, done.
